text:
maria: quick sync — i'm triaging a few Optimize docs regressions: broken python/node snippets, an obsolete quant name, and one internal link in the migration guide. planning to bundle small fixes into one PR. can folks pledge owners for snippets + smoke checks?

kevin: i can own the sdk snippets (node + py). drop filenames and i'll update patterns to the new client API.

maria: thanks. faulty files i flagged: docs/optimize/recipes/batching.md, docs/optimize/snippets/kv-prefetch-example.md, docs/optimize/migration/quant-mapping.md. node example in kv-prefetch uses old callback style and wrong param names.

kevin: noted. i'll rewrite node to the concise async SDK pattern and refresh the comment headers. example i'll replace it with: 

```js
// node: kv prefetch example (updated)
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const out = await client.optimize.generate({
  model: 'redwood/latency-v1',
  input: 'extract key points:',
  optimize: { batchSize: 4, kvPrefetch: true }
});
console.log(out.text);
```

anya: heads up — migration doc still mentions "quant-lite" and "quant-pro". we standardized names last quarter (q4_0, q5_0, q8_0). i'll add a compact mapping table and short guidance sentence recommending a quick eval before rollouts.

maria: please add a one-line note about potential differences in tokenization/profile behavior too.

anya: added mapping + note in my branch. mapping snippet: 

```
quant-lite -> q4_0
quant-pro  -> q5_0
quant-hq   -> q8_0
```

and a short sentence: "Run a focused eval on representative prompts after migrating quant profiles; small quality differences are expected and may require picking a neighboring profile."

kevin: pushed node + python snippet updates to my branch. python had an import path and deprecated method call — switched to RedwoodClient.optimize.generate(...) and normalized param names. sample: 

```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('RW_KEY'))
resp = client.optimize.generate(model='redwood/latency-v1', input='...', optimize={'batch_size':8, 'kv_prefetch':True})
print(resp.output)
```

sam: i can run the playground smoke for both snippet variants. what perf buckets should i record? median ms/token, p95, and repeated-token reduction for prefix caching.

maria: yes, please capture median, p95, throughput, and repeated-token reduction. aim to include a small example table in batching.md to illustrate tradeoffs.

sam: running now. my smoke command: 

```bash
# smoke harness for optimize playground
python -m redwood.tools.optimize_smoke --profile q4_0 --batch 4 --warmup 3 --runs 20
```

sam: quick results: batch=4 median 175ms/token, p95 260ms/token. batch=8 median 215ms/token, p95 340ms/token. throughput improved ~1.8x at batch 8. kv prefetch reduced repeated token compute by ~33% on our test set. logs attached.

kevin: perfect. i'll update batching.md with a short explanatory paragraph and embed sam's numbers with a caution: "numbers depend on model, sequence length, and runtime config."

maria: also found linkcheck flagged an internal-only bench url in docs/optimize/migration/quant-mapping.md. docs-bot, can you confirm which link is broken?

.docs-bot: Linkcheck output: 1 failing link -> /internal/bench/q5_0_perf (404). Recommend replacing with public summary or pointing at the model catalog entry.

maria: decision: remove internal link and add a short public-facing summary of perf expectations for q4_0/q5_0 (two lines). i'll draft and push that to the PR.

anya: i've added the mapping + the migration advisory. also added a tiny troubleshooting bullet: "If latency regresses after migrating quant, try q5_0 or verify tokenizer alignment."

kevin: opened a combined PR with my snippet fixes + anya's mapping + maria's link removal. left one inline about wording in batching.md. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4499

sam: quick review done, left a nit on phrasing around "throughput vs latency" bullets. not blocking.

maria: will address the nit and merge after CI passes. thanks all for the quick turnaround. i'll tag the release notes team to include a single line about docs clarity updates.

kevin: thanks. i also bumped snippet-lint rules where necessary to avoid false positives on optimize examples.

docs-bot: PR #4499 opened by kevin — checks: snippet-lint, linkcheck, unit-tests queued. CI status will post back here.
